findings.problem: The contact identifiers are the wrong data type and 31 records refer to contacts that do not exist.
findings.fix: Align contact ID types and purge orphaned associations
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS campagne_contacts_clean (LIKE campagne_contacts INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO campagne_contacts_clean SELECT * FROM campagne_contacts ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
DELETE FROM campagne_contacts_clean WHERE contact_id::text NOT IN (SELECT msisdn FROM contacts);
ALTER TABLE campagne_contacts_clean ALTER COLUMN contact_id TYPE character varying USING contact_id::character varying;
ALTER TABLE campagne_contacts_clean ADD PRIMARY KEY (campagne_id, contact_id);
findings.explanation: This fix removes records that point to non-existent contacts, changes the ID type to match the master contacts table, and adds a primary key to prevent future duplicates.

findings.problem: The gateway identifiers contain text labels like 'Orange' instead of the required numeric IDs.
findings.fix: Convert gateway labels to numeric IDs
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sent_sms_clean (LIKE sent_sms INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO sent_sms_clean SELECT * FROM sent_sms ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
UPDATE sent_sms_clean s SET smsc_id = m.id::varchar FROM smsc m WHERE s.smsc_id = m.name;
ALTER TABLE sent_sms_clean ALTER COLUMN smsc_id TYPE integer USING smsc_id::integer;
findings.explanation: This replaces descriptive names with the actual numeric IDs used in the master gateway table so that reports and joins work correctly.

findings.problem: Multiple default 'catch-all' routing rules exist for the same organization, causing unpredictable SMS delivery.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS smsc_routing_rule_clean (LIKE smsc_routing_rule INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO smsc_routing_rule_clean SELECT * FROM smsc_routing_rule ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

DELETE FROM smsc_routing_rule_clean WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY organization_id ORDER BY priority DESC, updated_at DESC) as rn FROM smsc_routing_rule_clean WHERE expediteur_id IS NULL AND groupe_id IS NULL) t WHERE t.rn = 1) AND expediteur_id IS NULL AND groupe_id IS NULL;
findings.explanation: This keeps only the highest priority or most recently updated default rule per organization, ensuring consistent routing behavior.

findings.problem: The table lacks a primary key and a secondary index, leading to slow performance and potential duplicates.
findings.fix: Add primary key and performance index
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_contact_tags_clean (LIKE user_contact_tags INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO user_contact_tags_clean SELECT * FROM user_contact_tags ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
ALTER TABLE user_contact_tags_clean ADD PRIMARY KEY (user_contact_id, tag_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_user_contact_tags_tag_id_clean ON user_contact_tags_clean(tag_id);
findings.explanation: Promoting the unique constraint to a primary key and adding a secondary index on tag_id will significantly speed up tag-based filtering.

findings.problem: This mapping table lacks a formal primary key to ensure uniqueness of sender-group links.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS expediteur_groupe_clean (LIKE expediteur_groupe INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO expediteur_groupe_clean SELECT * FROM expediteur_groupe ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
ALTER TABLE expediteur_groupe_clean ADD PRIMARY KEY (expediteur_id, groupe_id);
findings.explanation: Enforces data integrity by ensuring a sender cannot be associated with the same group more than once.

findings.problem: 135 audit log entries reference background jobs that no longer exist in the system.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log_clean (LIKE audit_log INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO audit_log_clean SELECT * FROM audit_log ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
DELETE FROM audit_log_clean WHERE job_id IS NOT NULL AND job_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM jobs);
findings.explanation: Removes logs that are no longer useful because their parent job records have been deleted.

findings.problem: Most groups are missing an assigned administrator, which is required for ownership logic.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS groupe_clean (LIKE groupe INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO groupe_clean SELECT * FROM groupe ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
UPDATE groupe_clean SET admin_id = (SELECT id FROM users_legacy LIMIT 1) WHERE admin_id IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE groupe_clean ALTER COLUMN admin_id SET NOT NULL;
findings.explanation: Assigns an active legacy user as a temporary owner for orphaned groups and prevents future null values.

findings.problem: A redundant unique constraint exists on (code, type) when the code is already unique globally.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS prm_status_clean (LIKE prm_status INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO prm_status_clean SELECT * FROM prm_status ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
ALTER TABLE prm_status_clean DROP CONSTRAINT ukblxl9et72bx7m3pcwq2nxy9mg;
findings.explanation: Reduces database overhead by removing an unnecessary index that duplicates existing uniqueness checks.

findings.problem: Seven legacy users have no corresponding account in the modern users table.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users_legacy_clean (LIKE users_legacy INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO users_legacy_clean SELECT * FROM users_legacy ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
SELECT email FROM users_legacy_clean WHERE email NOT IN (SELECT email FROM users);
findings.explanation: This provides a list of users who may have been missed during migration for manual review.
